overview.title: Surf coast beyond the city
overview.p1: Taghazout grew from a fishing village into one of Morocco’s best-known surf spots. The vibe is casual: hostels, surf schools, smoothie cafés and a string of beaches with different breaks.
overview.p2: You can visit on a day trip from Agadir or stay several nights if surfing is the main goal. The coast road continues toward other small beaches and viewpoints.

food.title: Eat in Taghazout
food.p1: Cafés and simple restaurants serve surfers and day visitors — expect smoothies, grilled fish and international backpacker favourites alongside Moroccan plates.
food.li1: Beach cafés for drinks and snacks.
food.li2: Grilled fish when the catch is in.
food.li3: Smoothie and brunch spots in the village.
food.li5: Agadir restaurants if you return for dinner.

1.title: Getting there
1.desc: Shared grand taxi or private taxi from Agadir (≈20–30 minutes). Buses also run the coast road.

2.title: Surf
2.desc: Many schools rent boards and offer lessons — book in season.

3.title: Sun
3.desc: Little shade on the open beaches; bring SPF and water.

q1.question: How far is Taghazout from Agadir?
q1.answer: About 20–30 minutes by road north of the city.

q2.question: Do I need to surf to enjoy it?
q2.answer: No — many visitors come for the relaxed beach village atmosphere.

q3.question: Can I day-trip from Agadir?
q3.answer: Yes — very common. Start in the morning and return late afternoon.

q4.question: Is it good for beginners?
q4.answer: Several breaks and surf schools cater to beginners; ask locally which peak suits the day’s conditions.

q5.question: Where to stay?
q5.answer: Surf hostels, guesthouses and small hotels line the village; Agadir remains the base for more resort-style stays.
